For each nonempty budget line, sum its expense costs and count its expenses. Find the unweighted average of those line totals. Among lines above that average, return one row containing their average total, their combined expense count, and their average excess over the selected lines’ average total
queries:
WITH line_totals AS (
    SELECT b.budget_id,
           SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost,
           COUNT(*) AS expense_count
    FROM budget AS b
    JOIN expense AS e ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
    GROUP BY b.budget_id
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_cost) AS average_total
    FROM line_totals
)
SELECT AVG(l.total_cost) AS average_total,
       SUM(l.expense_count) AS combined_expense_count,
       AVG(l.total_cost - o.average_total) AS average_excess
FROM line_totals AS l
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o
WHERE l.total_cost > o.average_total

WITH line_totals AS (
    SELECT b.budget_id,
           SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost,
           COUNT(*) AS expense_count
    FROM budget AS b
    JOIN expense AS e ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
    GROUP BY b.budget_id
),
selected_lines AS (
    SELECT total_cost, expense_count
    FROM line_totals
    WHERE total_cost > (SELECT AVG(total_cost) FROM line_totals)
),
selected_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_cost) AS average_total
    FROM selected_lines
)
SELECT AVG(s.total_cost) AS average_total,
       SUM(s.expense_count) AS combined_expense_count,
       AVG(s.total_cost - a.average_total) AS average_excess
FROM selected_lines AS s
CROSS JOIN selected_average AS a
